_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average price index of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice benchmarked to 2015 (indexed at 100), currently stands at 132, indicating a 32% rise since 2015. This increase is notable but not uniform across components, reflecting a recent and uneven climb in commodity prices. The index aggregates these key soft commodities relevant to breakfast consumption globally. However, the overall rise does not imply a steady trend across all items or time periods.
notes.movers: The largest contributors to the price increase are coffee and orange juice, with coffee up 93% and orange juice up 22% since 2015, while wheat and sugar have risen more modestly by 7% and 5%, respectively. These shifts are primarily driven by weather-related events and crop diseases, such as frost and drought affecting arabica coffee regions and citrus greening plus hurricanes impacting orange juice supplies. These markets are relatively thin and volatile, which means prices can move sharply on localized production shocks rather than broad inflationary pressures.
notes.why: This pattern illustrates how a few weather-exposed soft commodities can disproportionately influence headline indices like the breakfast basket. Given the nature of these thin markets, disruptions may sustain elevated input prices for years, reflecting structural vulnerabilities rather than general economic inflation.
